items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: I was playing with a fellow by the name of Oscar Young. We played over there in the park.

ctx.x: I used to practice that, see, because that's what they used to have said.

Oh, you can make high notes, but you can't make no low notes. And some father said, well, you can make low notes, and you can't make no high, see. So I fought hard to get both, see. And sometimes I would catch myself and be playing a melody or something like that, and make that high note and drop down. And I noticed that, you know. I'd say, no, that's easier to do. If you get the ambusho for it, you know, you can do it just, look like, without the least effort, see. We played a dance once. We played a dance over…
I said, well, I'll just go to the ground.
